C0.quote: We study approval-based committee voting from a novel perspective.

C1.quote: randomized voting rules that satisfy ex-ante neutrality, monotonicity, and continuity
C1.note: Main results are properties (neutrality, monotonicity, continuity/stability bounds, EJR+) of randomized rules. Polynomial-time algorithms and a dynamic low-recourse reduction are AL.

C2.1.value: approval profile; approval sets; ballots; voters' preferences
C2.1.quote: A collection of all voters’ approval sets is denoted by 𝐴

C2.2.quote: An approval set of voter 𝑖 ∈ 𝑁 is a subset

C2.3.quote: a voting rule selects a 𝑘sized subset (the committee) using voters’ preferences
C2.3.note: The only held-attitude term is 'voters' preferences', used as a synonym for the input. Elsewhere the input is described as approvals or ballots.

C2.4.quote: a voting rule selects a 𝑘sized subset (the committee) using voters’ preferences
C2.4.note: Doubt between IDU and ONE. The input is mostly called approval sets or ballots, but the rule is once described as applied to preferences directly. IDU is listed first.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers misreporting. Strategyproofness is mentioned only as a motivation for differential privacy.

C4.1.note: No voter utility, welfare, satisfaction, cost or distortion is used. The only use of 'utility' in Appendix C.1 refers to the dummy candidate ⊥, not to voters.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: We now define the standard proportionality axioms Justified Representation (JR)
C5.1.note: Results evaluate rules by JR and EJR+ (proportional representation of voter groups).

C5.2.quote: a committee 𝑊 provides 𝛼-EJR+ if there is no candidate
C5.2.note: Proportionality is defined on the approval sets submitted, with no statement relating them to held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: which we interpret to be the set of candidates that are “approved”

CAN.note: Candidates serve only as alternatives to be chosen.

OTH.quote_behav: the sequence 𝐸 is fixed at the outset
OTH.note: Adversary presenting the sequence of elections in the dynamic model. It is assumed oblivious, so its sequence is fixed.

C7.1.quote: We will assume an oblivious adversary.
C7.1.note: Both present types (voters and the adversary) are non-strategic.

C8.1.note: NA: no type is STRAT or MIXED.

claims.quote: proportional representation ensures that voters are adequately represented in the outcome
which we argue is favorable from the candidate perspective
it is also useful for guaranteeing voter privacy

C9.2.note: The claim that voters are adequately represented requires that submitted approvals reflect voters' held attitudes, and this is not stated. The privacy claim concerns votes themselves and needs no such assumption.
